# Indonesia coal power phase-out plan at risk due to stalled international funding

By Sudarshan Varadhan

November 17, 2025 5:35 PM UTC Updated November 17, 2025

- Partnership pledged $20 billion, but disbursal is slow
- Indonesia's JETP approved $2.85 billion in loans, no coal retirement yet

BELEM, Brazil, Nov 17 (Reuters) - Indonesia's plan to retire 6.7 gigawatts of coal-fired power plant capacity by 2030 to fight climate change is at risk of failure due to stalled disbursal of funding from rich countries, the country's top official overseeing the program told Reuters.
